Preliminary information regarding the accident was received at PS Jaitpur through DD No. 112A dated 21.01.2025 at about 11:51 PM, upon receipt of which, IO ASI Gulzar Ahmad along with HC Dalip immediately proceeded to the spot of accident at Bombay Expressway, Meethapur Chowk, near Durga Builder, Jaitpur where they found one motorcycle bearing registration no. Meanwhile, information was also received regarding the admission of injured persons at AIIMS Trauma Centre.

IO accordingly reached AIIMS Trauma Centre,
where he obtained the MLCs of the injured Naveen and Anas.
The MLCs recorded the alleged history as "RTA - 2W Non-Helmeted Rider hit by 4W at Meethapur."
Consequently, FIR was registered under the relevant provisions of the Bhartiya Nyay Sanhita.
PCR caller Rohit Singh was contacted during the investigation.

He stated that on 21.01.2025 at about 11:50 PM, while returning from Faridabad to Jaitpur after attending a marriage ceremony, he noticed a gathering at Durga Builder,
Meethapur Chowk.
On reaching there, he found a motorcycle and a rehdi in a damaged condition as well as two injured persons lying on the road.
He immediately called at 112 and then left for his home.
He categorically stated that he had not witnessed the mode or manner of the accident.

Notice under Section 133 of the Motor Vehicles Act was served upon the owner of the offending vehicle, namely Smt. Pooja Ponia who informed that her husband, Sh. Deepak Chaudhary (R-1), was driving the offending vehicle.
The documents of the offending vehicle were seized and verified from the concerned authority, and were found to be in order.

3. Reply/ Response:
3(a).
In response to DAR, Written Statement / Reply was filed on behalf of R-1 & R-2 who stated that they have falsely been implicated in the present case as no such accident took place.
It is stated that vehicle no. HR 51CN 8295 was duly insured on the date of accident hence any liability to pay compensation is specifically denied.
Other general defences were taken.
3(b) No reply to the DAR was filed on behalf of the Insurance Company.
However, it is pertinent to note that the Insurance Company has already settled the connected claim case of injured Naveen Kumar Singh in MACT No. 352/2025.
This fact itself indicates that the Insurance Company does not have any statutory defence available in the present matter.

5. Before putting in frame the position of law, it is noted that the process of determining the compensation by the court is essentially a very difficult task and can never be an exact science.
Perfect compensation is hardly possible, more so in claims of injury and disability.
(As observed by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Sidram Vs. The Divisional Manager United India Insurance Company Ltd, SLP (Civil) No. 19277 of 2019).

Measure of damages cannot be arrived at by precise mathematical calculations.
It would depend upon the particular facts and circumstances, and attending peculiar or special features, if any.
Every method or mode adopted for assessing compensation has to be considered in the background of "just" compensation which is the pivotal consideration.

Though by use of the expression "which appears to it to be just", a wide discretion is vested in the Tribunal, the determination has to be rational, to be done by a judicious approach and not the outcome of whims, wild guesses and arbitrariness.. ..."

8. It is settled proposition of law, as held in catena of judgments that "just compensation" should include all elements that would go to place the victim in as near a position as she or he was in, before the occurrence of the accident.

Whilst no amount of money or other material compensation can erase the trauma, pain and suffering that a victim undergoes after a serious accident, (or replace the loss of a loved one), monetary compensation is the manner known to law, whereby society assures some measure of restitution to those who survive, and the victims who have to face their lives.
